Emergency board, Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad and other carriers (disputes; signed 1960-04-22). The primary representation of the clause region is OCR-garbled (e.g. 'Presid(r) nt', 'oiadp k'); the clean second representation in OWN_TERMS carries the same two sentences, so the wording is read from there. Own terms: the board 'shall report its findings to the President ... within thirty days from the date of this order' and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, no change except by agreement 'from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report'. No termination clause, fixed end date, or earlier revoking, amending-away or superseding instrument found. Under the kit rule a report deadline is never an end, so EO 12553 is the first express end in held sources; but the board's operative effect plausibly lapsed by its own terms within about two months of signing (1960-04-22), so the reviewer should decide whether 12553 is the end or only a formal clean-up (upper bound). Later event changing the acting provision: no edge in either EDGES file targets EO:12553, no held order text amends or revokes it, and nothing in the dossier does.

Executive Order 10876
AMENDMENT OF EXECUTIVE ORDER  
NO. 10855,1  AUTHORIZING THE  
INSPECTION OF CERTAIN TAX RE­
TURNS
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by sections 55(a) and 508 of the Internal 
Revenue Code of 1939 (53 Stat. 29, 111, 
54 Stat. 1008; 26 U.S.C. 55(a) and 508), 
and by section 6103(a) of the Internal 
Revenue Code of 1954 (68A Stat. 753; 26 
U.S.C. 6103(a)), it is hereby ordered 
that the first paragraph of Executive 
Order No. 10855 of November 27, 1959, 
entitled “Inspection of Income Tax Re­
turns by the Senate Committee on the 
Judiciary”, be, and it is hereby, amended
(1) by deleting therefrom “ 1945 to 1958” 
and inserting in lieu thereof “ 1945 to 
1959”, and (2) by inserting therein “or 
Senate Resolution 238, 86th Congress, 
agreed to February 8,1960,” immediately 
after “Senate Resolution 57, 86th Con­
gress, agreed to February 2, 1959,”.
This order shall be effective upon its 
filing for publication in the F ederal  
R egister .
